title: Runbook
description: An operational procedure for one service, written before it is needed and tested on a schedule. It lives in docs/runbooks/<id>.md; `aidd doctor` warns when `tested_on` is older than `docs.max_runbook_age_days`.

title.description: One line: what the procedure does, such as "Fail over the orders database".

service.description: The service or system the runbook operates.

development_team.description: The development team that keeps the runbook current and answers its escalation. When the config has `development_teams`, `aidd validate` warns about a name that is none of its keys.

tested_on.description: The day a person last ran the procedure end to end, in a drill or for real. Absent means never tested.

restores_data.description: True when the procedure restores a stateful service's data from its backups (disaster recovery). `aidd doctor` then asks for `rto` and `rpo` and treats `tested_on` as the last restore drill, which it warns about when older than `docs.max_runbook_age_days`.

rto.description: Recovery time objective: the longest the service may be down before the restore completes: a number and a unit (m, h, or d), such as 4h.

rpo.description: Recovery point objective: the most data, as time before the failure, the restore may lose: a number and a unit (m, h, or d), such as 15m.

status.description: draft: written, not yet trusted. active: the procedure on-call follows. retired: kept for history; `aidd doctor` no longer checks its age.
